text.en:
Ria ran her fingers over a card of raised dots.
"It feels like a secret code," she said.

Braille is a way of reading and writing for people who cannot see. It uses patterns of raised dots that are read by touching with the fingertips.
It was created by Louis Braille, who lost his sight as a child. Each pattern of dots stands for a letter, a number or a sign.
The chapter shows how a clever idea can open the world of reading to many people. This summary is based on the well-known story or poem and on public chapter notes. Please read the exact text in the textbook, because the textbook version may differ in details.
